claims.text: Plain EXPLAIN plans the statement without executing it and prints the chosen plan: one summary line per plan node, sometimes followed by indented lines with details of that node.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: EXPLAIN (reference page); 14.1 Using EXPLAIN

claims.text: Without COSTS OFF each plan node shows cost=<estimated start-up cost>..<estimated total cost>, rows (estimated rows output by the node) and width (estimated average row width in bytes).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1.1 EXPLAIN Basics (the four numbers quoted by EXPLAIN)

claims.text: Plan costs are in arbitrary units set by the planner's cost parameters, not milliseconds; EXPLAIN ANALYZE's actual time is in milliseconds of real time, so the two are unlikely to match.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1.1 EXPLAIN Basics (arbitrary units); 14.1.2 EXPLAIN ANALYZE ('actual time' in milliseconds)

claims.text: The query planner estimates the cost of the plans it considers and chooses the one with the lowest estimated cost.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1 Using EXPLAIN (intro); 51.5 Planner/Optimizer

claims.text: A plan is a tree of plan nodes; child nodes are printed indented under their parent with a leading '->', and an upper node's cost includes the cost of all its child nodes, so the top line gives the estimate for the whole plan.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1.1 EXPLAIN Basics ('the cost of an upper-level node includes the cost of all its child nodes')

claims.text: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement and adds per node actual time (first row..all rows, ms), actual rows and loops (time and rows are per-execution averages when loops > 1), plus Planning Time and Execution Time lines.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1.2 EXPLAIN ANALYZE

claims.text: EXPLAIN ANALYZE discards the output a SELECT would return but other side effects happen as usual, so an UPDATE or DELETE changes data; running it between BEGIN and ROLLBACK leaves no change.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1.2 EXPLAIN ANALYZE (BEGIN; EXPLAIN ANALYZE ...; ROLLBACK;); EXPLAIN reference, Notes

claims.text: The planner estimates row counts from statistics collected by ANALYZE (and VACUUM ANALYZE) about each table's size and value distribution.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.2 Statistics Used by the Planner; 24.1.3 Updating Planner Statistics

claims.text: The autovacuum daemon, when enabled, issues ANALYZE on a table automatically once its contents have changed sufficiently; temporary tables cannot be accessed by autovacuum.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 24.1.3 Updating Planner Statistics; 24.1.6 The Autovacuum Daemon (temporary tables)

claims.text: When a condition is not selective (most rows qualify), a sequential scan can have the lowest estimated cost, so the planner uses it even though a usable index exists.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1.1 EXPLAIN Basics (selectivity examples); 11.1 Indexes Introduction

claims.text: In a bitmap plan the Bitmap Index Scan child visits the index to find the locations of matching rows, and the Bitmap Heap Scan parent fetches those rows from the table (heap = the table's own storage in PostgreSQL terms).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 14.1.1 EXPLAIN Basics (two-step bitmap plan); 73.1 Database File Layout (heap)

claims.text: The ANALYZE option of EXPLAIN only executes and measures the statement; it does not update planner statistics, which the ANALYZE command (or VACUUM ANALYZE, autovacuum) does.
